summary.text: Brandon Williams said there is “no question” the U.S. is in an AI capabilities race with China and that a five-to-seven-year procurement cycle would not keep up. In official statements, Williams described NNSA’s response to the Genesis Mission as immediate action to harness AI and ensure America continues to lead in AI and its critical applications. He said a proposed Amentum AI data center and energy project could strengthen U.S. AI leadership, reliable energy generation, and national security, and that working with the private sector can move faster and make productive use of federal land. Williams also said NNSA is combining AI, high-performance computing, and additive manufacturing to design and produce national security capabilities faster while keeping human judgment at the center.

statements.text: NNSA will use its computing power to take advantage of DOE’s world leading Genesis Mission, which unites three things America does better than anyone else: Artificial Intelligence (AI), advanced computing, and innovation, into a collaborative effort across government, industry, and academia to usher in a new golden age of scientific discovery. NNSA will invest in mission-enabling projects that are tailored to solve mission-specific challenges faster and with less power consumption than traditional computers to ultimately speed discovery, optimization, and manufacture of new materials and weapons designs.
